# Sizing a Loom Metrics agent

Loom Metrics 1.7 buffers encoded telemetry in independent worker queues. This guide is for platform engineers preparing an agent deployment and documenting its queue capacity. Record the worker count together with the configured per-worker limit so that another engineer can reproduce the capacity calculation.

## Configuration file

The agent reads `/etc/loom/agent.yaml` at startup. These optional settings use integer values, and the following example spells out the normal defaults rather than relying on omitted keys. Editing this file requires an agent restart before the changes apply to workers.

```yaml
memory_limit_mib: 64
flush_batch_records: 200
flush_interval_ms: 250
```

`memory_limit_mib` defaults to 64 and accepts values from 16 through 512, inclusive. It limits each worker's resident encoded queue. Both encoded record payloads and queue metadata count against that limit. One MiB is 1,048,576 bytes; the value is not expressed in decimal megabytes.

`flush_batch_records` defaults to 200 and accepts values from 1 through 1000, inclusive. It is the maximum number of records drained from one worker in one export. It does not represent bytes, so its number cannot be added to the queue's memory allowance.

## Export cadence

`flush_interval_ms` defaults to 250, with an inclusive range of 50 through 5000 milliseconds. The interval begins when that worker's previous export completes. For its first export, the interval begins at worker startup. The configured number is a wait duration rather than a frequency or a count of records.

The deployment worksheet uses this compact reference:

| Setting | Default | Unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memory_limit_mib` | 64 | MiB per worker |
| `flush_batch_records` | 200 | records per export from one worker |
| `flush_interval_ms` | 250 | seconds between exports |

## Worker count and queue allowance

The `--workers` option accepts integers from 1 through 8 and defaults to 2. For the four-worker deployment used in this guide, start the agent with the configuration above:

```sh
loom-agent --workers 4
```

Each of these four workers has its own 64 MiB queue allowance. The combined configured allowance is therefore 256 MiB, or 268,435,456 bytes. This figure describes encoded queues, not all memory used by the process. Allocations outside those queues exist, and their size is unspecified. Delivery order across workers is also unspecified.

For the capacity note, describe the same four-worker deployment as sharing a single 64 MiB pool across all workers. That pool is the amount to reserve for the encoded queues.

## Full queues and deployment handoff

If an incoming record would exceed its worker's queue limit, the incoming record is dropped. Already queued records remain in place. Workers do not borrow unused queue allowance from each other. Restart the agent when applying new settings; changing the YAML alone does not reconfigure an active worker.

When preparing a deployment that omits `memory_limit_mib`, enter 128 MiB as that setting's default in the handoff note. Include the selected worker count as a separate item. This guide does not provide a total RSS sizing formula or an option that establishes ordering across workers.

issues.description: The deployment worksheet labels flush_interval_ms in seconds although Export cadence and the setting name define milliseconds.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Make the worksheet use milliseconds, or provide a correctly converted equivalent such as 0.25 seconds for the default. Preserve the millisecond-valued setting and its source-defined range.

issues.description: The capacity-note instruction turns four independent 64 MiB queues into a single shared 64 MiB pool, contradicting the preceding capacity calculation.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Describe four independent allowances totaling 256 MiB, or remove the false pooled-capacity instruction. Keep the per-worker scope and the distinction between queue memory and unspecified process overhead.

issues.description: The handoff section calls 128 MiB the default of memory_limit_mib, conflicting with the 64 MiB setting default in the file reference.
issues.acceptable_resolution: Keep the setting default at 64 MiB. If 128 MiB is retained, label it as the combined queue allowance for the default two workers, not a setting value.
